title: Glue Job Failure - agentic-dev-customer-etl-pipeline (Customer ETL Pipeline)
description: Standard remediation for the agentic-dev-customer-etl-pipeline AWS Glue job. Classifies the failure from the CloudWatch 'Failure Reason' log content before acting - only a connection-refused error is safe to auto-retry; anything else needs human review.
match_rule: Match on the literal substring 'connection refused' (case-insensitive) appearing ANYWHERE within the log event's Failure Reason / error message text. This is a substring match, not a root-cause diagnosis: if 'connection refused' appears even as part of a longer explanation (e.g. 'connection refused: required upstream table is currently locked by another job'), that STILL counts as a match for this rule and the action is retry_glue_job. Do not withhold the match just because additional context follows the phrase.

example_log_events.description: Real GlueETLJobExceptionEvent - matches the connection-refused rule
example_log_events.raw_event:
{"Event": "GlueETLJobExceptionEvent", "Timestamp": 1783513907401, "Failure Reason": "Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/customer_etl.py", line 19, in <module>
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: connection refused: required upstream table 'customer_raw' is currently locked by another job. Retry once the lock is released.", "script": "customer_etl.py"}
example_log_events.why: The Failure Reason contains the literal substring 'connection refused', so this classifies as case A below and is safe to auto-retry, even though the message goes on to explain a table lock rather than a network-level connection failure.

decision_tree.name: Classify the Glue job failure from the Failure Reason log content
decision_tree.instruction: Read the 'Failure Reason' field (or equivalent error/exception text) from the job's CloudWatch log event. Check whether the substring 'connection refused' appears anywhere in it - see match_rule above for exactly how to apply this.

conditions.if: Failure Reason contains the substring 'connection refused' (case-insensitive, anywhere in the text)
conditions.note: Per policy this is treated as a transient/retryable condition regardless of the specific explanation that follows (network refusal, table lock, etc.) - safe to retry the job as-is.

conditions.if: Failure Reason does NOT contain 'connection refused' (e.g. schema/data errors, OOM, permissions, unknown)
conditions.note: Non-matching failure - root cause must be reviewed by data engineering before retrying, since a blind retry would likely fail again the same way.

decision_tree.name: Verify retry outcome
decision_tree.instruction: After retry_glue_job runs, confirm the job reaches SUCCEEDED. If it fails again, do not retry a second time automatically.

conditions.note: Retry did not resolve it - repeated failures indicate a persistent issue (e.g. the upstream lock is still held), not a one-off transient blip. Escalate.

feedback_notes: Only the literal substring 'connection refused' triggers auto-resolution by design - this is a simple, deterministic keyword rule, not an independent root-cause diagnosis. It intentionally also covers cases like upstream table locks that phrase their error as 'connection refused: ...', since a single retry is cheap and safe even if the true cause needs a second look after a repeat failure (see step 2). All other error patterns (schema mismatch, out-of-memory, permissions, data quality) require human review because a retry alone will not fix them.
